hero.oneLiner: HIL positions itself as a diversified, 30+ year infrastructure player spanning EPC Infra, an asset-light OMT Tollway Collection business, and Real Estate, with a government-heavy order book and a deliberately deleveraging balance sheet.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Diversified infrastructure business across three verticals - EPC Infra, Tollway Collection, and Real Estate - with 30+ years of execution experience, presence across 11 states and 1 union territory, and 105+ completed / 25+ ongoing projects.
- Tollway Collection runs an OMT (Operate-Maintain-Transfer) model that is asset-light with low working capital requirement, quick scalability across toll plazas, and ~Rs 1,000 Cr single-project bid eligibility; traffic growth flows directly to profitability with no construction risk and low incremental operating cost.
- EPC order book is weighted 64.9% public sector vs 35.1% private sector, a deliberate tilt toward government clients for better execution certainty and payment security.
- Describes itself as among the few tollway operators managing collection using advanced technologies with minimum revenue leakage.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Debt-to-equity improved from 0.9x (FY23) to 0.5x (FY26), alongside Net Worth growth from Rs 74.8 Cr (FY23) to Rs 228.5 Cr (FY26).
- FY26 return ratios: ROE 18.4%, ROCE 15.4%; PAT grew at a 32.1% CAGR from Rs 13.8 Cr (FY23) to Rs 31.8 Cr (FY26).
- Stated priorities: further improve the debt-to-equity ratio to create headroom for growth, improve return ratios through efficient capital deployment, and utilise net cash & cash equivalents toward working capital requirements.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body: - [Industry Tailwind] Deck cites sector-level growth drivers: MoRTH allocated Rs 3.10 lakh crore (Union Budget 2026-27, +8.0% YoY) with NHAI allocated Rs 1.87 lakh crore for FY27; India's toll collection is projected to roughly double from ~Rs 55,000 Cr to ~Rs 1.4 lakh crore within 2 years; government plans to introduce Multi Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection by end of 2026 (source: ET, CareEdge, IBEF, Business Standard, NPCI).
